Introduction to Tabular Data and Microsoft Excel

Lesson 3: Navigating Excel: Ribbons and Tabs

There are many useful tools and functions that you can access through Excel’s many tabs and ribbons. We want you to be aware of a few different ribbons, ahead of the next lessons, as we will be using them, because they can be overwhelming or confusing for first time Excel users.

Let’s click on two of the tabs in the top bar. Start with the home tab.

A diagram of the top ribbon in Excel.

The Home tab has many different interfaces. What is most important in this bar are the typographic options, the number settings, and the ability to add new rows and columns. This tab in the top ribbon has the most general functions, and it looks very similar to the Home tab in Microsoft Word. You may spend a lot of time using this tab when you start using Excel, but there are a few other tabs that are worth being aware of: the Formulas, Data, and View tabs.

The tab allows you to access information about different Excel formulas , and the View tab helps you change the way users view the spreadsheet. We will not be going into detail about these ribbons in this lesson.

Click on the Data tab. We will use some functions found in this tab later in this lesson. This ribbon includes some pre-defined functions that can help automate some otherwise time-consuming practices.

The Data tab can be used to access functions that are especially helpful for making it easier to process data. We will be using the ‘Text to Columns’ and ‘Data Validation’ tools later in this lesson.

We will be using the data tab later in this lesson. Before we do that, we need to learn the basics of formulating and executing equations in Excel.

Key Terms

Excel Sheets

A sheet is a unique single-page spreadsheet that is part of a larger collection of spreadsheets. They can be accessed at the bottom left side of the Excel interface.

Functions in Excel

Functions in Excel are pre-programmed processes that allow users to do complex match, data analytics, and data transformation in their workbooks. These functions often take structured inputs—in the form of numerical data, strings, or data from one or more cells—and output new information into the cell containing the function based on those inputs. They can use used to automate data throughout your spreadsheet.
